fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Revolutionary Behind the Method", "body": "New Chronology did not begin with Anatoly Fomenko. The episode traces its astronomical dating, dynastic parallelism and linguistic reinterpretation back to Nikolai Morozov, who in 1880 published a fourteen page pamphlet called The Terrorist Struggle, openly calling himself and his cohorts terrorists and championing political assassination over mass revolution. In the crackdown after Tsar Alexander II was assassinated in 1881, Morozov received a life sentence, spent some twenty five years in solitary confinement, and left Shlisselburg Fortress with twenty six volumes of manuscripts. His seven volume Christos, published between 1924 and 1932, became the blueprint Fomenko adopted, tweaked and pushed toward a far greater compression of history."}, {"title": "Revelation as a Storm and a Horoscope", "body": "Morozov reads the Book of Revelation as an eyewitness account of a thunderstorm woven together with astronomical observation, a primitive horoscope calculated by its author for one significant day, and he even reconstructs the hour the thundercloud passed and the rainbow appeared. The episode grants that Revelation is steeped in astrotheology, yet argues that knowing a text is astrological is not the same as knowing exactly what its author intended, since everything in the sky can be read more than one way. Morozov settles on September 30, 395 AD, partly because Revelation mentions the Lord's day, while Fomenko lands on October 1 or 2, 1486."}, {"title": "Do the Four Horsemen Really Mean Planets?", "body": "The dating scheme rests on reading the Four Horsemen as planets ridden by constellations: the white horse with a bow as Jupiter in Sagittarius, the red horse with a sword as Mars beneath Perseus, the black horse with scales as Mercury in Libra, and the pale horse of Death as Saturn in Scorpio. The episode points out that Perseus is not on the ecliptic, so Mars could sit anywhere from the end of Aries to the start of Gemini, and weighs a rival zodiacal reading in which wheat, scales, a sting and a bow trace Virgo, Libra, Scorpio and Sagittarius down into winter, the Hell that follows the pale rider."}, {"title": "Following the Evidence Back to Its Source", "body": "Morozov's drawing of a coin showing a horse ridden by a crab, offered as proof that ancient astrologers pictured planets as horses, turns up decades earlier in Antoine Fillioux's 1867 study of Gaulish coinage and in J.F. Blake's Astronomical Myths of 1877, and both read the horse as the Sun running between the solstice signs of Cancer and Capricorn, not as Saturn. Fomenko's own illustrations, including Jean Taisnier's 1562 planetary chariots, show deities riding in cars pulled by horses, eagles, doves and peacocks, and he drops in the Auriga constellation without explanation. A planet pulled by horses, the episode argues, is not a planet that is a horse."}, {"title": "Precise Math, Circular Meaning", "body": "Fomenko calls his 1486 result an independent astronomical dating, yet the episode argues the proposed date seems to shape the interpretation rather than the other way around, since no outside method of dating corroborates it. Even granting that horses equal planets, nothing in the colors fixes which horse is which planet. Fomenko also writes that Morozov's biblical readings escaped doubt, but in 1907 Vladimir Ern accepted the arithmetic while rejecting the identifications, calling it a question of philology rather than astronomy and asking where even the faintest shadow of proof could be found. A calculation can be precise while the reading fed into it is wrong."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Is Fomenko’s New Chronology legit? Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio investigate the evidence behind Anatoly Fomenko’s radical claim that much of ancient history actually happened in the Middle Ages. In Inner Whirled 31, we put his astronomical dating arguments to the test and ask what would justify rewriting the historical timeline.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: What if the Book of Revelation was written during the Renaissance, and the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse contain a date hidden in planetary symbolism? We explore Nikolai Morozov’s influence on New Chronology, compare his interpretation with Fomenko’s proposed date of 1486 AD, and follow the argument from biblical passages to astronomical reconstruction. Can these methods uncover a verifiable historical date? How much depends on the assumptions used to interpret the text?

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Planet Colors That Never Agreed", "body": "New Chronology needs the white, red, black and pale horses of Revelation to be Jupiter, Mars, Mercury and Saturn, so Chance tests that palette against the oldest color systems he can find. The Enuma Anu Enlil tablets give Marduk white, Nergal red and Ninurta black, while Ishtar and Nabu share warqu, a pale yellow green; Plato's Myth of Er paints Jupiter whitest and Mars ruddy on the Spindle of Necessity; the Papyri Graecae Magicae trade colors for stones and hand Jupiter a blue kyanos. Only Jupiter white and Mars red keep recurring, while Mercury black never turns up at all."}, {"title": "A Papyrus With No Find Spot", "body": "Before trusting any planetary stone list, Chance pauses on provenance. PGM XII surfaced through Giovanni Anastasi, a consul general in Egypt who sold antiquities to European museums, and nobody can say where it was dug up. His rule of thumb is that the brightest red flag for forgery is an artifact with no archaeological controls that perfectly fills a gap historians are hungry to close, here the leap from Neoplatonism to Renaissance ceremonial magic like the Key of Solomon. He stops short of calling it fake, noting only that it appeared in a golden age of forgery, unlike a second papyrus with a recorded 1922 excavation."}, {"title": "Zechariah's Horses and Morozov's Chapter Six", "body": "Chance hunts every precedent for planets as horses: the Vishnu Purana harnesses colored horses to planetary chariots, the Avesta turns Sirius into the white horse Tishtrya, and a Bruttian coin sets the Dioscuri on horseback, yet none makes a planet the steed. Morozov's Zechariah argument fares worse. He calls the four chariots of Zechariah 6 a reworking of the apocalypse partly because both passages sit in chapter six, though chapter divisions came from Stephen Langton around 1205, and his readings of Joshua as Jesus, the branch as John and the stone as Peter loop back to prove the Christian origin they assumed."}, {"title": "Thucydides and the Impossible Eclipse", "body": "Thucydides looks like a fairer test because he writes as an eyewitness and logs three eclipses, but his first one breaks the rules, a crescent sun with stars showing, which would need a partial and a total eclipse at once. The second is a modest partial eclipse in early spring, and the third is a lunar eclipse off Sicily that spooks Nicias into waiting thrice nine days while the Syracusans trap the Athenian fleet. Fomenko moves the whole war to 1133 CE, Dylan reads the eclipses as a plot device, and Chance notes the full text first surfaces in the hands of the Medici."}, {"title": "Would a Fake Eclipse Story Match Anyway?", "body": "Fomenko asserts that an invented eclipse triad would probably find no match in the sky, and Chance tests that claim. An AI search of the eclipse catalogs returns AD 1133, 1140 and 1151 if the first eclipse was total and 431 BC if it was partial, so the astronomy cannot choose. Claude played forger, and its invented triads found a real match within a 1,000 year span 82 percent of the time with totality required and over 99 percent with a lenient first eclipse, and GPT reached the same verdict by another route. Dylan adds that the Greek manuscripts funnel through Constantinople, possibly as priestly writings never meant as history."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Mercury being black is like a never, and Saturn being pale is also not supported at all.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Everybody who's looked at ancient history with a skeptical mindset will concede that the chronological record is a mess. It's like patched up guesswork based on patched up guesswork.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "We're talking about how a few pieces of work support a giant branching out of re-dating all kinds of things.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "No text is a true history. It's all a written account that is at best missing some stuff, at worst, making mistakes or fabrications.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "It's like I want to see this in a movie, but it just doesn't read like a historical account.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Either it's totally eclipsed and some stars come out, or it's partial eclipse, it's a crescent, and no stars come out.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The least reliable piece of evidence is testimony. The most reliable is hard physical forensic evidence, and most of our history is based on the witness stand testimony.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I think what you have is this mythological imperialism is a product of that modern Middle Ages, late Middle Ages, going into the Renaissance.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Modern historians actually think that they have verified the date of the Peloponnesian War by the very same means that Fomenko and Morozov are using to dispute it, which is the eclipses that Thucydides describes.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "It's basically a guarantee that an invented eclipse pattern would have some kind of match in the whole span of history.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Mainstream historians won't bother, they just dismiss it out of hand with ridicule, and conspiracy theorists that support the idea, they're kind of too lazy to bother.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Those four horsemen are the four seasons of the year.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Everything in the sky has more than one version of itself in the sky. There's more than one way to read it.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "It appears to me that these early texts are not as early as they pretend to be.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I just don't see how the actual text of Revelation supports going that far into a specific reconstruction.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The Tartaria emerging to the forefront is more of an indication of where the population is at.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Showing that the planet is in a chariot pulled by horses is not the same thing as establishing that the planet is the horse.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "If you're relying on other people being credible, that's an actual limited supply. And you can only have so many people on your show bringing their credibility before they've exhausted everything.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "You have the interpretation informing a proposed date, or is it a proposed date informing an interpretation?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The more effort you have to put into something to decide whether it's talking about something in the historical record or not, that is your answer.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I legitimately came into this just wanting to know if new chronology has anything to it.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Can you not just make any statistical chart look the way you want it to look based on the parameters that you make the intervals on the chart?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
